title: Make planner settle open questions and callers before the critic
summary: Tighten the planner prompt and plan template so a plan settles every criterion-affecting open question, lists callers and tests per changed production path, and names where each new dependency comes from. Athena refuses a plan with an unresolved criterion-linked open question before the critic runs, and the critic brief shows user-accepted deviations. The audience is the planner and critic roles, plus the maintainer judging plan quality.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for the refusal and the brief sections; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria check that the refusal and the critic section actually occur, via tests that run.
The open-question rule is enforced in plan_findings, not by prose alone.
Prompt text and doc comments are written for an outside reader.
One focused change to the planning pipeline; the queued cap item is excluded.
A verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
The template and prompt change, and an Athena check enforces it, instead of only a prompt note.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The plan template is PlanOutput in crates/athena-context/src/outputs.rs, with its stored form JobPlan in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs. The planner instructions are crates/athena-context/prompts/planner.md.

Open questions become structured: each can name the acceptance criterion number it affects (optional). A question tied to a criterion that is still unresolved makes the plan invalid. Resolved items move into decisions, so a plan that passes review has no such question.
The refusal is a major Athena finding in admission::plan_findings, which already sends a plan back to the planner without a critic call. That matches 'refused before review'.

New template fields: per changed production path, a list of callers and tests with a still-passes verdict (a failing test must also appear in files); and a source for each new dependency at each entry point.

Accepted deviations are passed to the critic brief as a new section, and critic.md is told not to re-raise them. Source assumed to be the accepted reading or request text and docs/decisions.md. If the repository has no existing record of accepted deviations, the producer uses the minimal available source and records the call.
No governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) need to change.

acceptance_criteria.text: crates/athena-context/prompts/planner.md tells the planner to settle every open question and every 'producer to check' item that affects an acceptance criterion before submitting, to list existing callers and tests for each changed production path with whether each still passes, to put any breaking test into files or change the design, and to state where each new dependency comes from at each entry point.

The plan template (PlanOutput and the stored JobPlan) has fields for per-path callers/tests with pass status and for new-dependency sources per entry point, and open questions can name the criterion they affect. The brief's plan rendering (plan_body) shows these fields.
critic_brief gets a section that lists the deviations the user has accepted, and prompts/critic.md tells the critic not to raise them again.

A new test shows that a plan whose open question is tied to an acceptance criterion and is unresolved yields a major Athena finding from plan_findings, so it is refused before the critic call, while the same plan with the question resolved or not tied to a criterion yields no such finding. Run: cargo test -p athena-core admission.

A test shows that the critic brief contains the accepted deviations section when deviations are given, and that the planner brief and plan rendering include the new fields. Run: cargo test -p athena-context.

Existing tests still pass after the template change, including the job_plan CLI tests and the fake-agent plan fixtures, with clippy clean and cargo fmt --check passing. Run: cargo test, cargo clippy, cargo fmt --check.

out_of_scope: Keeping the last plan when the planning round cap is reached (queued item planning-cap-reached-job-fails-no-plan-kept)
Changes to the critic's severity rules beyond not re-raising accepted deviations
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows
departures: Wider than the reference: the change touches the output schema, the stored record, the admission gate and two prompts, and the source of 'accepted deviations' is ambiguous. Cost, time and pass-rate are shifted accordingly.
hard_reason: It changes the plan-review gate (plan_findings) that judges other jobs, and the stored JobPlan record shape.
